_TLDR: It’s better when those in power use it to reflect the world in which we all actually live._

We’ve got a couple layers to this reflection, so stay with me as we make our way up and out. I’m joining a new team soon, so I took a break between jobs to look up at the Texas sky, ponder, drive, and find my new center.

I’m settling into my design lead era. Not just as a title, but as a way of being. Less responsive. More proactive. Less about proving myself or the work. More about guiding teams and embodying the role. I can literally say this ain’t my first rodeo and I got the anecdotes to prove it.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 3](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*MT2fI08k252rSfOPn3PseA.png)

Naturally, my perspective as a leader is shaped by those that have led me and it just so happens that most of them are in Texas now. Now felt like the right time for a check in. After our time together this visit, I realized that the inner circle I’ve built over the years consists of bad-ass, high-level women with impeccable taste.

They have shaped me, stuck by my side, and continue to create pathways for me. I could never have gotten to where I am in my career if it weren’t for them.

So I want to honor their work on me (because Lordy knows I need it) by sharing what they’ve exemplified to me over the years. Each embodies a kind of power that’s not performative, nor is it loud until necessary. These powers are deeply integrated into who they are and their creative practice. I’d like to share them with you.

### _The Power of Remaining Cool_

There is a kind of calm that isn’t passive. It’s deliberate, almost watchful. The kind of calm that patiently waits for your at-level teammate (who truly should get it by now) as they catch up by talking it through live on the team call.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 4](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*h-AnleuUHpDttwjoMkFU5Q.png)

The ability to stay composed when things are tense, unclear, or unraveling is a form of leadership in itself. It sets the tone for others, creates space for better decisions, steadier conversations, and more thoughtful outcomes. Remaining cool doesn’t mean disengaging; it means refusing to let urgency dictate judgment.

In a working world that often rewards reaction and speed, this kind of calm is radical.

### The Power of Trust and Team-Building

Trust, when extended early and genuinely, has a compounding effect. It shifts how people show up. It creates clear stepping stones for teammates to own and then clear signals when steps are missed.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 5](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*WBzMi---wOrr79Lb3fDfzg.png)

Trust transforms people just doing stuff together competing for validation and getting paid, into teams that support each other and have your back because they care.

Thoughtful team-building isn’t about control, it’s about belief. When people feel trusted, they take ownership. When they feel supported as they grow, they stay. This kind of leadership builds momentum that outlasts any single project, performance review, or employer.

### The Power of Creative Confidence and Play

Creative confidence doesn’t always look like certainty while doing the thing. Sometimes it looks like curiosity. Sometimes it looks like attentive listening. Sometimes it looks like a willingness to explore without overprotecting the outcome. And sometimes it looks like diving into the ball pit or jumping the fence to hit a late night slide.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 6](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*MGO4lwVsNZ0ncY6lwaW9tA.png)

When we approach creativity with openness to the creative spirit rather than fear of the unknown, we make better outcomes.

Play has been perverted by the world of work. Your maker didn’t make you be a step in the production process or to just push pixels. Play and creativity and human-centric design have been positioned like a luxury which, maybe one day, we’ll be able to afford or have the freedom to experience. When in reality, they are foundational to who we are as people and a non-negotiable in the human experience.

### The Power of Empathy

Speaking of God, I saw a piece of writing in Houston that I haven’t been able to escape. It read:

_“If God answered the prayers you’ve been praying, would it change anyone else’s world or just your own??”_

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 7](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*p4FuncVegCTdNUqsVgWtVg.png)

Do with that what you will…

Empathy is often framed as softness, but in practice, it’s discipline of your emotions such that you can sense others’. And that’s tough. If there’s one thing most creatives (along with a few other professions) need right now, it’s self-discipline.

Empathy requires attention. Attention to people’s histories, work priorities, and emotional states, without losing clarity or direction. When empathy is present, decisions become more grounded. Next steps become clearer. Fewer assumptions are made. Expectations align. Conversations become more honest. KPIs get met. Win-win.

The work improves because it accounts for real human mindsets, not just abstract, green-pasture, fantasy-world scenarios.

### The Power of Perseverance

Last and most important of all: perseverance. Perseverance rarely announces itself. It shows up quietly, over time, through consistency and self-discipline rather than spectacle or promotion. It’s the decision to keep going when progress is slow, incremental, and recognition is delayed.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Image 8](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*UYIAPJiuiUutmFYYXWGOtw.png)

This kind of endurance builds credibility, depth, technical skill, and trust. Notice how all of the powers above ultimately live inside perseverance.

If you’re struggling, please keep going. Now is the time for your breakthrough.

These women hold different roles as marketing executives, managers, art directors, or studio practitioners. They come from different cultural and ethnic backgrounds; Texans born and raised, immigrants, second-generation Americans, Muslim, Jewish, Christian. They bring distinct lived experiences into every conversation they enter.

## Diversity isn’t decorative. It’s essential:

Two truths come to mind as we get out of this reflection. I will tease these. Both deserve so much more conversation than what I’ll write out here. But I have to aknowledge them. The first: DEI is under attack in the United States. The second: super-powerful AI systems are rapidly reducing the number of humans behind massive machines. Together, these truths mean the power and responsibility of leaders in our country is increasing exponentially. That those in power can do more with it than ever before.

Therefore, the call to action for myself and to all leaders stepping up to the plate: Growth and positive change doesn’t happen in isolation, and it doesn’t happen in sameness.

> Growth happens in difference.

Once more, slowly. Growth happens in difference. Different perspectives. Different strengths. Different weaknesses. It happens among others, especially communities committed to solving problems and seeking a north-star vision of their future.

As I step into this next chapter of my career, that feels like the real work: to model this way of being. That leadership is a group practice and it’s better when those in power, use their power to reflect the world in which we all actually live.

_Flowers for my inner circle: Jessica Destoppeleire, Jessica Rosenberg, Josie Jeffries, Meghan Glasgow, Molly Snowberger, Nancy Klokowski, Nancy McNee Newell, Tracy Arcabasso Smith, Zeinab Mohtadi, cmfw. A heartfelt thank you for guiding me over the years and for being generous with your time, wisdom, and power._
